Hi Liang — thanks for flagging this, and sorry for the confusion.

Short answer: Calendly usually auto-detects timezones, but some corporate Outlook setups and browser locale settings (or an intermediate proxy in your network) can cause the ICS to be interpreted in UTC or with the wrong zone. Two quick fallbacks we use:

1) I can send a manual .ics that pins the meeting in UTC (and include the equivalent local time in the body) so your calendar doesn't rely on the Calendly UI.
2) Alternatively, if you open the Calendly page and use the timezone dropdown (bottom-left), you can force it to "(GMT+08:00) Hong Kong" before booking — that usually fixes it.

If you prefer, propose three fixed times (with time zone) and I'll send the ICS from our side. Example slots in UTC:
- 2028-11-03 00:00 UTC (08:00 HKT)
- 2028-11-03 02:00 UTC (10:00 HKT)
- 2028-11-03 04:00 UTC (12:00 HKT)

Which one works? If you're okay, I'll loop in Marissa to send the invite file directly.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
